title: Access recertification worklog and SIEM field mapping
content:
Purpose:
This is the working log for the Q1/Q2 quarterly least-privilege recertification run. It captures decisions made while validating RBAC v2 role bindings, the audit-log schema fields we rely on for evidence, notes about automating evidence collection, and the SIEM export mappings used by SOC for verification. This doc is intentionally informal — design notes, TODOs, and command snippets are expected.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: org-level privileged roles, service accounts used by CI/CD, Dedicated cluster admin roles, and cross-account IAM roles used by Private deployments.
- Audience: security-and-compliance, eng-platform (RBAC owners), SRE, and SOC analysts who validate access evidence.

Summary of current state (quick bullets):
- RBAC v2 rollout completed across prod/dedicated, but there are ~18 outstanding role bindings flagged as "legacy-admins" by the RBAC scanner.
- Audit logs now emit expanded fields (see AuditLogSchema v2 below) but our SIEM ingest drops some tokenized fields; needs remap.
- Evidence automation prototype (scripts/recert/collect_evidence.py) collects access grants and recent use for accounts, but does not yet attach full request payload samples due to PII policy.

Owners and SLAs:
- Recert run owner: Maya Chen (security).
- RBAC remediation owners: engineering team leads (list in Confluence page linked).
- SOC verification window: 10 business days after recertification snapshot is published.

Planned timeline for next quarterly run (compressed):
- T-21 days: Freeze role changes, announce recert window to teams (Slack channel #sec-recert).
- T-14 days: Run RBAC scanner (rbac-v2/scanner) + initial false-positive suppression pass.
- T-10 days: Publish recert snapshot to S3 (s3://redwood-recert/q2-2026/snapshot.json) and kick evidence collection job.
- T-7 days: Teams review and respond via form (internal link).
- T-0: Finalize revocations/justifications and update policy-branch for infra automation.

Checklist for reviewers (what counts as evidence):
- "Grant exists" evidence: current role_binding record plus the owning service/team and purpose statement.
- "Recent use" evidence: at least one successful access event within the last 90 days (audit log event id + timestamp).
- "Justification" evidence: ticket/PR link, or signed business justification in the recert form.
- "Owner confirmation": explicit owner email or group confirmation.

AuditLogSchema v2 (fields we depend on):
- timestamp: ISO8601 string of event time.
- event_id: UUID v4 string.
- actor_type: string (user | service_account | system).
- actor_id: canonical id (email or service account id).
- actor_roles: comma-separated role ids at time of event (RBAC v2 role ids).
- action: canonical action (e.g., iam.grant, iam.revoke, deployment.create, secret.access).
- resource_type: string (cluster | deployment | secret | api_key).
- resource_id: stable resource identifier.
- request_payload_hash: SHA256 of redacted request payload (for correlation without PII).
- outcome: allowed | denied | error.
- request_context: short string with client_ip and region (redacted by policy).
- trace_id: optional trace id for cross-service correlation.
- policy_evaluation: abbreviated result (pass | fail | NA) with rule id

Notes on schema quirks:
- actor_roles is currently emitted as an array in the raw logs; SIEM ingest flattens arrays to a single comma string — downstream queries must split on comma.
- request_context is truncated to 256 chars on older nodes; prefer the new collector version.

SIEM export mapping (current implementation vs desired):
- Current: logs -> s3 partitioned by day -> log-forwarder transforms keys (lowercases everything), then sends to SIEM with fields: time, src, msg, severity.
- Desired: direct mapping (best-effort) to fields used in AuditLogSchema v2. Example mapping we want to implement in log-forwarder config:
  - siem.time = timestamp
  - siem.event_id = event_id
  - siem.actor = actor_id
  - siem.actor_type = actor_type
  - siem.actor_roles = actor_roles
  - siem.action = action
  - siem.resource = resource_id
  - siem.outcome = outcome
  - siem.trace_id = trace_id

Splunk example queries (SOC playbook snippets):
- Find role-grant events for legacy-admins in last 30 days:
  index=audit_logs action=iam.grant actor_roles="*legacy-admin*" | stats count by actor_id, resource_id
- Identify service accounts that never had successful use in 90 days:
  index=audit_logs actor_type=service_account earliest=-90d | stats count by actor_id | where count=0
- Snapshot export for recert evidence (CSV):
  index=audit_logs AND (action=iam.grant OR action=secret.access) earliest=-365d | table timestamp,event_id,actor_id,actor_roles,action,resource_id,outcome > /tmp/q2-evidence.csv

Evidence automation notes (scripts and outputs):
- scripts/recert/collect_evidence.py currently:
  - reads snapshot.json, queries audit API for events per actor_id between snapshot_date-365d and snapshot_date, and collates evidence.json (list of event ids + minimal metadata).
  - writes evidence package to s3://redwood-recert/q2-2026/evidence-packages/<team>.tar.gz
- Known gaps:
  - Collector rate limits cause incomplete pull for very large orgs; workaround is paging with backoff (implemented but needs tuning).
  - Some events have request_payload_hash not present when requests exceeded 10KB; need to adjust collector sampling config.
  - The script does not yet attach the Confluence justification links automatically (manual step).

Remediation/automation proposals (short list):
- Add a "recert:owner_email" tag to RBAC bindings so automation can auto-email owners and auto-populate justification links.
- Update log-forwarder (v1.9) to send actor_roles as a CSV field under siem.actor_roles and preserve original array under meta.actor_roles for deep-dive flows.
- Add a nightly job to precompute per-account "last_seen" metric to avoid expensive historical queries during recert windows.

Playbook: Quick runbook for an auditor verifying a single binding:
1) Open snapshot.json and find binding for subject X. Confirm binding metadata (role id, created_at, owner tag).
2) Pull evidence package for owner/team from S3 and open evidence index.
3) In SIEM, run event query for actor_id X earliest=-365d to collect 1) grant event, 2) any use events.
4) If no use events: check scheduled jobs and service account metadata (jobs may be out-of-band). If still none, escalate to owner for justification or revoke.
5) Record final decision in the recert form and attach evidence CSV + short note.

Unresolved questions / risks:
- PII policy prevents including full request payloads; does the SOC need payload fields for certain incident triages? If yes, we need a gated retrieval flow.
- Some private deployments are configured to forward logs to on-prem SIEM with different field schemas; need per-customer mapping docs.
- RBAC scanner false-positive rate for templated infra roles (~6%) — need whitelisting mechanism.

Meeting notes (2026-02-18 sync):
- Decided to pilot actor_roles CSV mapping with SOC on next recert run. Samir to own forwarder change.
- Lina will prototype owner-tagging automation as a GitHub Action that adds recert metadata when role bindings are created.
- Rahul will scope PII-gated request retrieval flow and list required approvals.

Next steps before finalizing run:
- [Samir] merge forwarder mapping PR and run in staging (deadline 2026-02-28).
- [Lina] land owner-tagging action and backfill missing owner tags for high-risk roles (deadline 2026-03-04).
- [Maya] publish snapshot and kick the evidence collector for a dry run (deadline 2026-03-05).

Appendix: useful commands and quick links
- Run local evidence collector: python3 scripts/recert/collect_evidence.py --snapshot s3://redwood-recert/q2-2026/snapshot.json --out /tmp/evidence.json
- S3 viewer: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/buckets/redwood-recert (internal-only)
- Slack channel: #sec-recert (use thread with subject tag recert-q2-2026)

-- end of working log --
